prompt: Daily high temperatures in a city, measured in Celsius, have standard deviation $2.5^\circ$C. Converted to Fahrenheit with $F = 1.8C + 32$, what is the standard deviation of the Fahrenheit temperatures?
hint: The formula multiplies each temperature by $1.8$ and then adds $32$. Only one of those two steps changes how spread out the values are.

hints.text: The formula multiplies each temperature by $1.8$ and then adds $32$. Only one of those two steps changes how spread out the values are.
Adding $32$ shifts all values together, so ignore it. For $Y = aX + b$ the rule is $\sigma_Y = |a| \cdot \sigma_X$, so compute $1.8 \times 2.5$.
$1.8 \times 2.5 = 4.5$, so the standard deviation is $4.5$ degrees Fahrenheit.

explanation: Standard deviation measures spread, and adding $32$ slides all values together, so it leaves the spread alone.
Multiplying by $1.8$ stretches every gap between values by a factor of $1.8$, so the standard deviation is stretched the same way.
So $\sigma_F = 1.8(2.5) = 4.5$, a standard deviation of $4.5$ degrees Fahrenheit.

alternativeExplanations.title: Follow two days
steps: Suppose two days are $20^\circ$C and $22.5^\circ$C — one SD apart.
The gap went from $2.5$ to $4.5$, so the SD did too.
